summary: Target-level continuation of the inherited L1 plan: quantitative unbounded Amice inversion, analytic substitutions and operator continuity, support-sensitive division, radius-loss primitives, and the topology behind derivative/logarithm nonsplitting. Existing targets and bounded-measure APIs are imported rather than assigned duplicate nodes. All targets are planned; the L0 topology/carrier input is requested explicitly and no implementation closure is claimed.

conventions.field: p is a prime, including 2. Unless explicitly broadened, K is a finite extension of Q_p with the absolute value extending |p|=p^(-1). L/K used for torsion is a finite extension with the extending absolute value. This pass makes no assertion for arbitrary affinoid coefficients or for arbitrary complete coefficient fields.
conventions.radii: r and s are positive real norm radii. Closed-disc analytic series satisfy |a_n|r^n→0. R+ consists of native PowerSeries K satisfying native IsRestricted r at every 0<r<1; q_r(F)=PowerSeries.gaussNorm norm r F. A cofinal increasing sequence r_j→1 gives its Frechet topology. Colmez uses valuation radii u, related by r=p^(-u).
conventions.stages: LA_h is imported from L0 with normalized residue-disc coordinate (x-a)/p^h and maximum Gauss norm. D is its locally analytic strong dual, not AbstractMeasure on continuous functions. Write ||μ||_h for the Banach-dual restriction norm. LC_h comprises functions constant on residue classes modulo p^h.
conventions.derivatives: D_T is native PowerSeries.derivative. ∂=(1+T)D_T is the existing PMIA Mahler derivation, never a second definition. Function differentiation is d_x. The distribution derivative is the POSITIVE transpose dμ(f)=μ(d_x f), so A(dμ)=log(1+T)Aμ. Coordinate multiplication instead gives A(xμ)=∂Aμ.
conventions.substitution: F(z(1+T)-1), with |z-1|<1, means convergent analytic substitution. It is not native formal substitution with a nonzero constant. F((1+T)^a-1), a∈Z_p, has zero inner constant and agrees with formal substitution after restrictedness is proved.
conventions.support: Support on a clopen U means μ(f)=μ(1_U f) for every analytic test f. Unit reciprocal means the locally analytic function equal to x^(-1) on units and zero on pZ_p. It is not a reciprocal at zero.
conventions.primitive: Function primitives are unique modulo LC(Z_p,K). On R+ the ordinary normalized T-primitive is continuous; the ∂-primitive is unique modulo K. Neither statement supplies a continuous section of d_x on LA, or a right inverse of the positive distribution derivative.

declarations.provides: Native radius-restrictedness predicate; no new power-series carrier.
Coefficient norm decay under atTop exactly matches the open-disc membership condition.
Native real coefficient supremum, used only on restricted series where it is bounded.
Explicit boundedness condition for the native conditional real supremum.
Existing formal derivative as a Derivation over a commutative semiring.
Coefficient n is (n+1) times coefficient n+1.
Over a torsion-free commutative ring, equal derivatives and equal constant coefficients imply equality.
Native characteristic-zero formal series log(1+T); analytic convergence is new, not its coefficients.
Formal identity D_T(log)(1+T)=1, over a commutative Q-algebra.
Native coefficient constructor for the light normalized primitive formula.
Existing bounded-measure coefficient transform; its carrier is not the strong locally analytic dual.
Bounded transform coefficients evaluate Mahler functions, matching the unbounded inclusion.
Integers in Q_p have norm at most one; normalized coefficient fields inherit this estimate.

Source declaration for the complete nonarchimedean summability criterion, with the generated additive theorem NonarchimedeanAddGroup.summable_of_tendsto_cofinite_zero. The source-based index lists the multiplicative declaration; the additive generated form is used for scalar pairings.

Injectivity of the bounded transform over a complete ultrametric normed Z_p-algebra with bounded scalar action; its native source statement was read and applies to normalized finite coefficient fields.

nodes.title: The open-disc Frechet algebra
nodes.statement: Define R+(K) as the subalgebra of native PowerSeries K with IsRestricted r F for every real 0<r<1. Equip it with the topology generated by q_r, not the coefficient product topology or the radius-one norm. It is a complete Hausdorff metrizable locally convex K-algebra; every cofinal increasing sequence of radii tending to one gives the same topology. Polynomials are dense.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Take the intersection of native restricted subrings; each coefficient projection is bounded by r^(-n)q_r.

Realize this topological algebra as the compatible inverse limit of weighted Gauss c0 Banach algebras on a cofinal countable set of radii; completeness is coordinatewise completeness plus Gauss convergence. These Banach carriers are imported from L0.
Truncation converges in every q_r by restrictedness. No identity with all analytic point functions or new rigid disc geometry is needed.
acceptance: The geometric series belongs to R+ but is not restricted at radius one.
Convergence of T^n to zero in each q_r is compatible with dense polynomials; it gives no uniform radius-one convergence.

sources.match: Open-disc coefficient growth and the Frechet Gauss topology; the inverse-limit adapter is worker planning.

nodes.title: Unbounded inverse Amice pairing
nodes.statement: For F=Σb_nT^n∈R+, construct μ_F(f)=Σa_n(f)b_n on LA(Z_p,K). At stage h, put d_h(n)=floor(n/p^h)! and c_n=a_n(f)/d_h(n); c_n→0. The values d_h(n)b_n are bounded, so the pairing is summable and |μ_F(f)|≤sup_n|d_h(n)b_n| ||f||_h. The maps agree on nested stages and μ_F(binomial(x,n))=b_n. Conversely any distribution is determined by these values.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Import Amice’s orthonormal basis d_h(n)binomial(x,n) from L0. Its dual is bounded coefficient families, not c0.

For every h choose valuation radius s with 0<s<u_h, u_h=1/((p-1)p^h). Since v_p(d_h(n))=n u_h−O(log(n+1)), the Gauss bound at p^(-s) gives v_p(d_h(n)b_n)→+∞; boundedness already suffices for the dual pairing.

The normalized test coefficients tend to zero, so their products with bounded dual values tend to zero. Complete ultrametric summability, uniqueness of Mahler coefficients and density of polynomials give compatibility and both inverse identities.

For an arbitrary distribution, the basis dual bound gives |b_n|≤||μ||_H/|d_H(n)|. For each 0<r<1 choose H with r<p^(-u_H); exponential radius decay dominates the factorial logarithmic error and gives native IsRestricted r. The inherited norm inequalities then compare cofinal Gauss radii and stage dual norms.
acceptance: A normalized basis vector has pairing d_h(n)b_n.
The forward transform of μ_F equals F coefficientwise.

sources.locator: Theorem I.4.7/Corollary I.4.8, p. 15; Theorem II.2.2 and proof, p. 30

nodes.title: Topology of the bounded-measure inclusion
nodes.statement: The canonical inclusion ι:M(Z_p,K)→D(Z_p,K) from bounded measures, equipped with their continuous-test Banach-dual norm, is continuous and injective, with ||ιμ||_h≤||μ|| for every h. Its image consists precisely of bounded Amice coefficient sequences, is dense in D for its strong Frechet topology, and is not closed. The coefficient square with native AbstractMeasure.amiceTransform commutes. This uses the inherited unbounded Amice isomorphism and the existing bounded inverse; it does not define a second bounded transform or replan the isomorphism.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: The norm-decreasing restriction LA_h→C(Z_p,K) gives the displayed transpose estimate. A zero restriction makes every Mahler value zero; native injective_amiceTransform then gives the zero bounded measure, proving injectivity without a new continuous-function Mahler theorem.

Native coeff_amiceTransform and the inherited distribution coefficient formula agree on every Mahler test. The PMIA bounded inverse identifies bounded coefficients with precisely the bounded-measure image; for finite K this is O_K[[T]]⊗_(O_K)K.

The inherited amice-dirac result and Gauss density of polynomials make the span of natural Dirac measures dense in D. Native log lies in R+ with unbounded coefficients, so the bounded image is proper and hence not closed. The Gauss/dual norm equivalence comes from the imported Amice theorem, not a new declaration.
acceptance: Aδ_0=1 and Aδ_1=1+T give genuine bounded-measure points of the inclusion.
dδ_0 transforms to log(1+T), outside the inclusion although in its closure.
The norm topology of bounded measures is not identified with the Frechet topology on the whole distribution space.

sources.match: Bounded coefficient subspace, unbounded transform and density of natural Dirac masses. The inclusion norm estimate and nonclosed-image conclusion are worker deductions.

nodes.title: Analytic affine substitution
nodes.statement: For F=Σb_nT^n∈R+, a,b∈K with |a|<1 and |b|≤1, define C_(a,b)(F)=Σ_n b_n(a+bT)^n by convergence in every smaller Gauss algebra. Its kth coefficient is Σ_(n≥k)b_n binomial(n,k)a^(n-k)b^k. For 0<r<1 and max(|a|,|b|r)<s<1, q_r(C_(a,b)F)≤q_s(F). This is a continuous K-algebra homomorphism R+→R+; evaluation is E(CF,t)=E(F,a+bt) when |t|<1. It coincides with native formal substitution when a=0, and polynomial substitution for polynomials.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Choose the strict intermediate s. The nth summand has q_r norm at most |b_n|s^n (max(|a|,|b|r)/s)^n; complete ultrametric Gauss convergence constructs the series.
Pass coefficient projections and native analytic evaluation through this convergent sum; polynomial identities pass by dense truncations.
The displayed norm inequality proves continuity. Nonzero a is handled by the infinite convergent sum, never by an unsupported formal HasSubst.
acceptance: For character twist use a=z−1,b=z with |z−1|<1; then |z|=1 and all stated domains hold.
No map is asserted if |a|=1.

nodes.title: Finite coefficient extension and descent
nodes.statement: For a finite extension L/K, scalar extension gives D(Z_p,L)≅L⊗_K D(Z_p,K) and R+(L)≅L⊗_K R+(K) as topological L-vector spaces, with Amice commuting with coefficient inclusion. These are finite-dimensional coefficient comparisons using a finite K-basis of L, not arbitrary completed tensor identities. If L/K is Galois, an element with invariant coefficients descends uniquely to K. Thus the finite root averages in inherited ball restriction descend to K even when individual roots are not in K.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Use a finite K-basis and equivalence of the coefficient norms to compare each LA_h(L) with a finite product of LA_h(K); L0 owns the scalar stage comparison.
Taking continuous duals and finite products gives the distribution comparison. The same finite-basis bounds compare all Gauss seminorms on R+.
The Amice coefficient equality gives compatibility; Galois permutes the roots and corresponding character terms, making the average invariant. Descent is coefficientwise with the same radius bounds.
acceptance: For L=K all maps are identity.
At n=0 the restriction average consists only of F and requires no extension.
For a rational Dirac distribution the root average has K-coefficients and equals either its transform or zero.

sources.locator: Corollary I.4.6, p. 15; Proposition II.4.1, p. 35

nodes.title: Differentiation and dilation on the open disc
nodes.statement: For F∈R+ and 0<r<1, D_TF and ∂F lie in R+ and q_r(D_TF)≤r^(-1)q_r(F), q_r(∂F)≤r^(-1)q_r(F). Both are continuous. For a∈Z_p, U_a(T)=(1+T)^a−1 has zero constant and q_r(U_a)≤r, so native formal substitution F(U_a) belongs to R+ and q_r(F(U_a))≤q_r(F). For a=p, q_r(U_p)≤max(p^(-1)r,r^p). The inherited dilation transform and PMIA Mahler derivation are used without redefining either.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Native coefficient differentiation and |n|≤1 give the derivative bound and restricted tail decay. Since q_r(1+T)=1, multiplication gives the ∂ estimate.
Integral binomial coefficients of a∈Z_p give U_a’s norm and zero constant. Summation of b_n U_a^n converges in the radius-r Gauss algebra, agreeing with native formal substitution.
For U_p use p divisibility of the intermediate binomial coefficients and retain the leading T^p coefficient.
acceptance: a=0 gives F(U_0)=F(0), not F.
For a=1 the substitution is the identity.
∂T=1+T, whereas D_TT=1.

sources.match: Coordinate differentiation and dilation identities; these quantitative Gauss bounds are worker deductions.

nodes.title: Normalized primitive on the open disc
nodes.statement: Define normalizedSeriesPrimitive F by constant coefficient zero and coefficient n+1 equal to b_n/(n+1). For F∈R+ it lies in R+ and D_T(IF)=F. For 0<r<s<1, q_r(IF)≤r(1−r/s)^(-2)q_s(F), so I:R+→R+ is continuous. Among R+ series it is the unique primitive with zero constant; all ordinary T-primitives differ by a K-constant.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: The real-bodied definition uses native PowerSeries.mk and division in the coefficient field.
In normalized p-adic norm, |1/(n+1)|≤n+1. Let ρ=r/s: each weighted integrated coefficient is at most r q_s(F)(n+1)ρ^n, and sup_n(n+1)ρ^n≤(1−ρ)^(-2). Using a still larger radius proves tail decay.
Native coeff_derivative proves the inverse equation, while derivative.ext supplies uniqueness. These Gauss bounds depend on a larger input radius.
acceptance: I(1)=T and I(T)=T^2/2, including p=2.
This is ordinary T-integration, not function-side d_x primitivation.

nodes.title: Hasse differentiation in an analytic stage
nodes.statement: For f∈LA_h, ||p^(hj) f^(j)/j!||_h≤||f||_h for every j≥0, and these normalized Hasse derivatives tend to zero in LA_h as j→∞. In particular ||d_x f||_h≤p^h||f||_h, and d_x:LA→LA is continuous. The estimate is stated on test functions; its transpose is bounded with ||dμ||_h≤p^h||μ||_h.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: In residue-disc coordinate u=(x-a)/p^h, Hasse differentiation multiplies the shifted coefficients by integral binomial coefficients.
The supremum of coefficients with index at least j tends to zero, proving the asserted decay without dividing norm inequalities by a small factorial.
Apply the LF universal continuity property to the fixed-stage maps and transpose with the L0 strong-dual bounded-set interface.
acceptance: j=0 recovers f with its exact norm.
For f(x)=x, d_x f=1; there is no negative transpose sign.
A locally constant indicator has derivative zero in any stage resolving its conductor.

sources.match: The Hasse estimates used to make convolution’s intermediate evaluation analytic.

nodes.title: Convolution continuity on Z_p
nodes.statement: For f∈LA_h and λ∈D, y↦λ(x↦f(x+y)) is in LA_h with norm at most ||λ||_h ||f||_h. Consequently ||λ*μ||_h≤||λ||_h||μ||_h, and convolution on D(Z_p,K) is jointly continuous in its strong Frechet topology. Under inherited Amice it is multiplication on R+. This specializes the inherited general compact-group construction; no product tensor space is replanned.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Expand f(x+y) in each residue pair of normalized coordinates; translating by integral residue representatives does not increase the Gauss norm.
Use the Hasse stage estimates to expand the intermediate λ evaluation into a convergent normalized power series in y; applying the Banach dual bound gives the inequality.
Apply μ to that analytic test. The family of dual seminorm inequalities proves joint continuity, and evaluate characters to obtain the inherited convolution transform.
acceptance: δ_a*δ_b=δ_(a+b); δ_0 is the additive unit.
For dδ_0*dδ_0 the transform is log(1+T)^2, which is outside the bounded-measure subcase.

sources.locator: Lemma II.4.2 and Proposition II.4.3, p. 36
sources.match: Analytic intermediate evaluation and multiplication of transforms; the stage inequalities are read from that proof.

nodes.title: Restriction, twist, dilation and psi continuity
nodes.statement: For g,f∈LA_h, ||gf||_h≤||g||_h||f||_h and ||gμ||_h≤||g||_h||μ||_h. For U=b+p^nZ_p, restriction is multiplication by 1_U and has dual norm ≤1 at every h≥n. For z with |z−1|<1, choose h with z^x∈LA_h; multiplication by this fixed character is continuous on LA and D, and transforms through analyticAffineSubstitution_(z−1,z). Unit dilation σ_a is a stage isometry. For φ from x↦px, ||φμ||_h≤||μ||_h. The masked pullback Qf(x)=1_(pZ_p)(x)f(x/p) satisfies ||Qf||_(h+1)=||f||_h, hence ||ψμ||_h≤||μ||_(h+1). All these transposes are continuous for the strong topology; the inherited psi-projector identities therefore hold as continuous identities.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Multiplication and resolved clopen masks obey coefficient Gauss bounds. Use a common finer stage when the multiplier is not in the test stage. A continuous linear test operator sends bounded sets to bounded sets, which controls its strong transpose.

For characters, the Mahler series gives membership at an admitted radius; analytic-affine-substitution proves the transform formula. Pullback by a unit permutes normalized discs and acts by an integral invertible affine coordinate.

For dilation use the norm-decreasing affine chart map. For Q use the exact normalized chart identity of Colmez I.6.1; its zero extension is valid because pZ_p is clopen. Evaluate ψφ and φψ on analytic tests, importing their inherited definitions.
acceptance: ψδ_p=δ_1, ψδ_1=0, φδ_1=δ_p.
The case μ=δ_0 satisfies φψμ=μ and is not unit supported.
The ψ estimate changes h to h+1; no unsupported same-stage division-by-p bound is asserted.

sources.match: Multiplier, clopen restriction, dilation and the exact radius shift for masked inverse dilation.

nodes.title: Locally analytic reciprocal on units
nodes.statement: Let ι(x)=x^(-1) for x∈Z_p^× and ι(x)=0 for x∈pZ_p. This is in LA_1, with ||ι||_1≤1 and xι=1_(Z_p^×). Define Jμ=ιμ on unit-supported distributions. It is continuous on that closed subspace, supported on units, and xJμ=μ=J(xμ). Its underlying function is the inclusion into K of the PMIA extended PadicInt.inv, including zero on every nonunit.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: On a unit residue disc a+pZ_p expand (a+pu)^(-1)=a^(-1)Σ_(j≥0)(−p/a)^j u^j; its coefficients decay and are bounded by one. On pZ_p take zero.
Transpose this fixed analytic multiplier using inherited distribution-multiply and operator-stage-control.

The identity xι=unit indicator proves both inverse equations on the supported subspace. These two equations give uniqueness directly; on bounded inputs the same underlying reciprocal is the imported inverseWeight. The construction does not assume the inherited unit-division theorem that it supports.
acceptance: This does not provide x^(-1) at zero.
For arbitrary μ, multiplying Jμ by x gives the unit restriction, not μ.

nodes.title: Coordinate division and its ambiguity
nodes.statement: Coordinate multiplication x:D→D is surjective, its kernel is exactly Kδ_0, and all solutions of xλ=μ differ by Kδ_0. In transform coordinates solve ∂G=F by G=I(F/(1+T))+c, where division by the formal unit 1+T preserves R+. For a unit-supported μ, the analytic-unit-inverse solution is the unique unit-supported one and agrees with inherited division-on-units.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: The geometric series for (1+T)^(-1) lies in R+; multiply F by it and use the normalized primitive.
Amice identifies coordinate multiplication with the supplier Mahler derivation, so its kernel consists of constants by native derivative.ext. Constants transform back to Kδ_0.
Alternatively decompose every test as f(x)=f(0)+xg(x) with g locally analytic, proving the kernel directly. Unit support excludes δ_0 and selects J.
acceptance: ∂log(1+T)=1, so a solution of xλ=δ_0 is λ=dδ_0; it is not unit supported.
For δ_1 the support-selected solution is δ_1.

sources.match: Division by x corresponds to a primitive and has Dirac-at-zero ambiguity.

nodes.title: Primitives on smaller balls
nodes.statement: For a closed disc B(a,R) and a chosen strictly smaller concentric norm radius 0<r<R, define I_(a;R,r)(f) by coefficient integration with value zero at a. It is a continuous linear map from An(B(a,R),K) to An(B(a,r),K), satisfies d_x I(f)=f on the smaller disc, and ||I(f)||_r≤r(1−r/R)^(-2)||f||_R. In normalized residue coordinates u=(x-a)/p^h, a primitive on a smaller disc has an extra factor p^h. On LA_h choose primitives separately, normalized at each centre of residue discs modulo p^(h+1); this produces a continuous stage map LA_h→LA_(h+1). These maps are not asserted compatible as h varies.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Integrate coefficients in x-a, using the same p-adic reciprocal-integer and geometric-decay bound as the series primitive.
Restrict f from the original disc to a smaller disc around each new residue centre, then integrate in its normalized coordinate; the coordinate scaling gives the p^h factor where appropriate.

The finite clopen refinement patches these local primitives into LA_(h+1). If two primitives have equal derivative, their local analytic difference has no positive coefficients in characteristic zero, hence is locally constant. This supplies the inherited analytic-local-primitives theorem rather than assuming it.
acceptance: A primitive of 1 normalized at a is x−a.
For f=0, another primitive may be 1_(pZ_p), which is not a global constant.
Sparse f(T)=Σ_(m≥1)p^m T^(p^m−1) is restricted at radius one, but its zero-constant primitive has coefficient one at each p^m and is not restricted at radius one.

nodes.title: The topology of locally constant functions
nodes.statement: For finite K, LC=ker(d_x:LA→LA) with its induced topology is the strict locally convex inductive limit of LC_h≅K^(Z_p/p^hZ_p). Every bounded subset of LC lies in some LC_h, and each LC_h is closed in LC. The sequence 0→LC→LA→LA→0 is strictly exact; all three spaces are of compact type and reflexive. This is the Z_p application of L0 compact-type closed-subspace, exact-duality and strict-limit interfaces, not ownership of their general theory.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Hasse-stage-estimate makes d_x continuous and coefficientwise characteristic-zero differentiation identifies its kernel as LC.

Apply the requested L0 closed-subspace/inductive-limit comparison to the kernel: its intersection with LA_h is precisely LC_h, since an analytic function with zero derivative on a residue disc is constant there.

The L0 strict LF bounded-set theorem confines each bounded set to a finite level. Radius-loss primitives prove surjectivity; use the L0 open-mapping/strict quotient comparison for the compact-type spaces.
acceptance: 1_(p^nZ_p) belongs to LC_n, but not LC_(n−1) for n≥1.
The unit balls in all LC_h do not form one bounded total subset of LC.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.2 and Corollary 4.3, pp. 20–21
sources.match: The induced smooth-function topology is the strict finite-level limit, and differentiation has smooth kernel.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 1.2, p. 3; Corollary 1.4, p. 4

nodes.title: The bounded total set obstruction
nodes.statement: Let B be the image in LA of the norm-unit ball of LA_0. It is a bounded O_K-submodule whose K-linear span is dense in LA, since every polynomial lies in LA_0 and polynomials are dense in every LA_h. There is no continuous K-linear surjection LA→LC. Consequently there is no continuous projection LA→LC restricting to the identity on LC, and d_x has no continuous K-linear right inverse.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Continuity of LA_0→LA preserves boundedness, and K-linear scaling spans LA_0. Amice’s stage basis consists of polynomial functions, yielding density at every stage.

A continuous surjection q would send B to a bounded set with dense K-span in LC. The requested strict-limit bounded-set theorem puts q(B) in one closed finite-dimensional LC_h, contradicting the increasing conductor functions.

If S is a right inverse of d_x then P=1−S d_x maps into LC, is identity on LC and is continuous as an LA-valued map; the subspace topology makes it continuous as an LC-valued surjection. This contradicts the preceding obstruction.
acceptance: A conductor-n indicator outside LC_(n−1) witnesses infinite dimension.
Existence of continuous stagePrimitive maps does not supply compatible global S.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.2 and Corollary 4.3, pp. 20–21
sources.match: The bounded total lattice versus finite-level boundedness obstruction. The worker specializes to Z_p and finite K, using its ordinary Mahler basis; the paper’s general-group scalar-extension reduction is not needed.

nodes.title: Duality and the logarithm quotient
nodes.statement: Under Amice and the positive transpose derivative, the strong dual of 0→LC→LA→LA→0 is 0→R+ --multiplication by t--> R+→LC′_b→0, with t=log(1+T). It is strictly exact, tR+ is closed, and R+/tR+≅LC′_b topologically. The quotient sequence has no continuous K-linear section. Multiplication by t is injective with inverse continuous on its image; it is not surjective onto R+.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Import strict compact-type duality and reflexivity from L0; the locally-constant comparison supplies the strictly exact function sequence.
Use inherited amice-derivative to identify the positive transpose with t multiplication. Strictness identifies the image topology, closed image and strong-dual quotient.

A continuous quotient section would give a complementary projection and, after transpose and bidual identification, a continuous projection LA→LC; bounded-total-obstruction rules it out. No coefficient extension to Cp or unsupported general completed tensor theorem is inserted.
acceptance: t has zero constant, so 1 is not in tR+.
The range tR+ has its subspace topology, not a guessed single Gauss norm.
The normalized ordinary T-primitive does not split this logarithm quotient.

sources.match: The function and Frechet logarithm exact sequences and their nonsplitting.

nodes.title: Logarithm on torsion-translated discs
nodes.statement: The native formal t=PowerSeries.log K lies in R+. For z∈L with |z−1|<1 and ξ^(p^n)=1, |ξ−1|<1, log ξ=0 and E(t,ξz−1)=E(t,z−1); equivalently analyticAffineSubstitution_(ξ−1,ξ)(t)=t. The actual function in the layer is log(ξ(1+T)), not log applied to a formal expression without convergence. At T_0=ξ−1, log(1+T) has a simple zero: its derivative there is ξ^(-1)≠0.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: The nth logarithm coefficient has norm at most n, so n r^n→0 for r<1; native derivative_log_mul_one_add_X determines the derivative of its analytic evaluation.

Every p-power root reduces to one in the residue field, hence has |ξ−1|<1. The convergent logarithm is additive on 1+the open unit ball, as in Colmez I.6; p^n logξ=log1=0 and characteristic zero gives logξ=0.

The convergent affine substitution domain is valid since |ξ|=1. The logarithm identity follows pointwise and also coefficientwise by differentiating the analytic substitution and evaluating its constant; use coefficient uniqueness rather than identifying arbitrary point functions with rigid sections.
acceptance: ξ=1 gives zero at T=0 and derivative 1.
p=2, ξ=−1 gives zero at T=−2 inside the 2-adic open disc.
At |T|=1 no logarithm convergence is claimed.

sources.match: The convergent logarithm law, its vanishing on torsion, and the torsion translate formulas; simple-zero conclusion is a worker deduction.

nodes.title: Removal of logarithmic apparent poles
nodes.statement: For F∈R+(K), after a finite extension containing ξ of p-power order, let T_0=ξ−1. Locally near T_0, F/log(1+T) extends analytically iff E(F,T_0)=0, because the denominator has a simple zero; the extended value is ξ times the local derivative of F at T_0. In the guaranteed global case F=Aν with ν=dμ, F=tAμ, the quotient extends on the entire open disc as Aμ, including every such point. No assertion that arbitrary F vanishing at all torsion points is globally divisible is required here.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Expand both analytic functions in the local coordinate T−T_0. The logarithm is (T−T_0) times a local unit with constant coefficient ξ^(-1).

A zero value of F makes its local expansion divisible by T−T_0; the converse follows by evaluation. This local unit inversion can be obtained by a smaller-disc geometric series, without an unproved global Weierstrass divisor theorem.
For ν=dμ use the inherited exact transform identity, so Aμ is already the analytic extension globally. Descent uses the finite coefficient comparison.
acceptance: F=t has quotient 1 and extended value 1 at every torsion zero.
F=1 has a pole at T=0.
F=T has local quotient value 1 at zero but, for p=2, is nonzero at T=−2 and cannot have a global quotient in R+.

sources.match: Logarithmic derivative and torsion evaluations; the local simple-zero cancellation criterion is a worker deduction.

nodes.title: Negative moments and primitive ambiguity
nodes.statement: For m≥1, k≥1, and b∉p^mZ_p, let U=b+p^mZ_p. If H is any k-fold ∂-primitive of Aμ in R+ (∂^kH=Aμ), then μ(1_U x^(−k))=p^(−m)Σ_(η^(p^m)=1)η^(−b)E(H,η−1). The test 1_U x^(−k) is extended by zero off U and is locally analytic, even when U consists of nonzero nonunits. Any two choices of H differ by a polynomial of degree ≤k−1 in t=log(1+T); the root average annihilates this ambiguity. The formula is not asserted for a ball containing zero.
hypotheses: Standing normalized finite-extension field, radius and topology conventions.
proofSteps: Repeated coordinate division constructs a ∂^k-preimage; in a neighbourhood of zero use t as a local coordinate with ∂t=1, so ker(∂^k) consists of degree<k polynomials in t. Subtract this polynomial globally and use coefficient uniqueness (or inductively use ker∂=K) for the global assertion.
Apply inherited ball restriction to x^kλ=μ where Aλ=H. On U the factor x is invertible and 1_U x^(−k) is locally analytic, so the desired moment is λ(1_U).

At each torsion root t evaluates to zero. Only the constant ambiguity remains; the finite root character sum vanishes because b is nonzero modulo p^m. Use the supplier prime-root-power-sum iteratively, or the same finite geometric identity for p^m.
acceptance: For μ=δ_1, U=1+p^mZ_p and k=1, the negative moment is 1.
For p=2, U=2+4Z_2, μ=δ_2 and k=1, the moment is 1/2; avoiding zero is weaker than unit support.
For U=p^mZ_p the test x^(-1) is undefined at zero and the constant ambiguity survives.

sources.match: Finite-root moment formula and independence of logarithmic primitive ambiguities on balls avoiding zero.

Heavy definitions and their global API/tests therefore live in the README; the compact Lean file checks only genuine native scalar milestones and light coefficient definitions.
